objectives.en: Define a tissue and a meristem
Distinguish apical, intercalary and lateral meristems
Explain primary and secondary growth in terms of meristems

narration.en: Cows graze a lawn down to stubs, yet within a week the grass is tall again. Grass has a growing zone at the base of its leaves that animals cannot easily eat.
narration.kn: ಹಸುಗಳು ಹುಲ್ಲನ್ನು ತೀರಾ ಕೆಳಗೆ ಮೇಯ್ದರೂ ಒಂದು ವಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತೆ ಎತ್ತರ ಬೆಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಹುಲ್ಲಿನ ಎಲೆಗಳ ಬುಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯ ವಲಯವಿದೆ.

body.en: A tissue is a group of cells with a common origin that usually perform a common function. In plants, growth is largely restricted to special regions of actively dividing cells called meristems. The cells produced by meristems later stop dividing and become permanent tissues.
body.kn: ಸಮಾನ ಉಗಮ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮಾನ ಕಾರ್ಯವುಳ್ಳ ಕೋಶಗಳ ಗುಂಪು ಅಂಗಾಂಶ. ಸಸ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ಸಕ್ರಿಯವಾಗಿ ವಿಭಜಿಸುವ ವರ್ಧನ ಅಂಗಾಂಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ (ಮೆರಿಸ್ಟೆಮ್) ಮಾತ್ರ.

points.en: Permanent tissue: cells that have stopped dividing

narration.en: A tissue is a group of cells with a common origin that usually perform a common function. In plants, growth is largely restricted to special regions of actively dividing cells called meristems. The cells produced by meristems later stop dividing and become permanent tissues.
narration.kn: ಸಮಾನ ಉಗಮ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮಾನ ಕಾರ್ಯವುಳ್ಳ ಕೋಶಗಳ ಗುಂಪು ಅಂಗಾಂಶ. ಸಸ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ಸಕ್ರಿಯವಾಗಿ ವಿಭಜಿಸುವ ವರ್ಧನ ಅಂಗಾಂಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ (ಮೆರಿಸ್ಟೆಮ್) ಮಾತ್ರ.

say.en: Meristems are zones of dividing cells. Picture a plant: shoot above the soil, root below.
Apical meristems sit at the tips of the shoot and the root; they make the plant longer.
Intercalary meristems, as at the base of grass leaves and internodes, regrow grazed parts.
Lateral meristems, the cambia, run along the sides and add girth.
Apical and intercalary give primary growth; lateral meristems give secondary growth.

body.en: Apical meristems occur at the tips of roots and shoots and produce primary tissues; the shoot apical meristem also leaves behind axillary buds. Intercalary meristems occur between mature tissues, as at the base of leaves and internodes in grasses, and help regenerate parts removed by grazing herbivores. Both appear early in life and their growth is called primary growth.
body.kn: ಅಗ್ರ ಮೆರಿಸ್ಟೆಮ್ ಬೇರು ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಂಡದ ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ. ಅಂತರ್ವೇಶಿ ಮೆರಿಸ್ಟೆಮ್ ಹುಲ್ಲಿನ ಎಲೆ ಮತ್ತು ಗೆಣ್ಣಂತರಗಳ ಬುಡದಲ್ಲಿ; ಮೇಯ್ದ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಮರುಬೆಳೆಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಇವು ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಗೆ ಕಾರಣ.

narration.en: Apical meristems occur at the tips of roots and shoots and produce primary tissues; the shoot apical meristem also leaves behind axillary buds. Intercalary meristems occur between mature tissues, as at the base of leaves and internodes in grasses, and help regenerate parts removed by grazing herbivores. Both appear early in life and their growth is called primary growth.
narration.kn: ಅಗ್ರ ಮೆರಿಸ್ಟೆಮ್ ಬೇರು ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಂಡದ ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ. ಅಂತರ್ವೇಶಿ ಮೆರಿಸ್ಟೆಮ್ ಹುಲ್ಲಿನ ಎಲೆ ಮತ್ತು ಗೆಣ್ಣಂತರಗಳ ಬುಡದಲ್ಲಿ; ಮೇಯ್ದ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಮರುಬೆಳೆಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಇವು ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಗೆ ಕಾರಣ.

body.en: Lateral meristems occur in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, especially woody ones, and appear later in life. The fascicular vascular cambium, the interfascicular cambium and the cork cambium are lateral meristems. They produce secondary tissues and increase the girth of the plant, which is secondary growth.
body.kn: ಪಾರ್ಶ್ವ ಮೆರಿಸ್ಟೆಮ್ ಪಕ್ವ ಭಾಗಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ: ನಾಳ ಕ್ಯಾಂಬಿಯಂ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾರ್ಕ್ ಕ್ಯಾಂಬಿಯಂ. ಇವು ದ್ವಿತೀಯಕ ಅಂಗಾಂಶ ರೂಪಿಸಿ ದಪ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: A farmer notices that his maize stems grow taller but his mango tree trunk also grows thicker every year. Which meristems explain each change?

steps.en: Growth in length at the tip comes from the apical meristem (with intercalary meristems at the internodes in grasses such as maize).
Growth in thickness of the mango trunk comes from lateral meristems: the vascular cambium and cork cambium.
So length = primary growth; girth = secondary growth.

answer.en: Height: apical (and intercalary) meristems; thickness: lateral meristems (cambium)
